subject: dsa
title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
summary: Even after rotation, one side of the midpoint is always sorted. Check whether the target lies inside that sorted side; if not, search the other side.
problem: A sorted array was rotated at an unknown pivot. Find the index of target.

steps.caption: This sorted array was rotated. Find 0, still in O(log n) time.
Search the whole range. The trick: compare the low end with the middle; whichever side is in order is the one we can reason about.
Mid is 7. Since low (4) <= mid (7), the left half [4..7] is in order. Is 0 inside that sorted range [4, 7]? No, so search the right side.
New range [4, 6]: values 0, 1, 2 are back in order.
Mid is 1. Again low (0) <= mid (1), so the left half [0, 1] is sorted, and 0 sits inside it. Search left: hi moves to 4.
lo and hi have met, leaving one cell at index 4.
Check it: it's 0. Found at index 4.
